defects: The horizontal desk form is restored, but the close capture still reads as a dark flat slab supported by generic box columns and rectangular feet.
Broad window and room reflections are largely absent from the smoked glass surface; the top is materially flat in the production lighting.
The two support joints, tabletop fittings, feet, and underside hardware lack the visible manufacturing construction of the photographed desk.
Godot measures the lower bound at Y=0.395 inches, leaving a small gap above the RoomScale floor datum.
hard_fail_reasons: A neutral viewer describes the candidate as simplified/blocky game or CAD geometry rather than realistic furniture.
The candidate fails close inspection because the tabletop, columns, feet, and hardware resolve as simple primitives with weak material/surface response.
The real source photograph's glass-and-metal character, broad reflections, dual-column connections, and detailed foot construction are not materially approached.
incumbent_comparison: V024 corrects the orientation failure in v023 and presents a recognizable standing desk with UV-mapped PBR slots, paired telescoping columns, and T-feet. Compared with desk-v007, it still reads as more generic block geometry, with substantially weaker glass reflections and less convincing joins, feet, and hardware. Preserve desk-v007 as current best-so-far; v024 is not promoted.
likely_causes: The bevelled-box reconstruction uses large primitive components and simplified rectangular supports instead of the photographed desk's nuanced radii, connection plates, cable path, and visible fasteners.
The glass shader and restrained noise maps do not reproduce broad reflected window/room structure under the existing compatibility renderer.

Cylinder components were authored on the default Blender local-Z axis while the assembly components use a Y-up convention, so levelers and fasteners are misaligned with intended horizontal surfaces; the leveler placement also misses the floor datum.
next_action_hypothesis: Refine the component-authored strategy using correctly oriented horizontal fasteners/levelers, a true zero-height floor contact, smaller glass-edge chamfers, physically clearer glass reflection/transmission, and material-specific roughness/normal detail. Add more faithful formed feet, mounting plates, telescoping transitions, and visible under-top support/cable hardware. Re-evaluate the same RoomScale views against the photograph and incumbent; reject if the result still reads as primitive geometry or lacks credible surface and manufacturing detail.

observations.art_direction_fit: The dark finish fits the workstation palette, but the generic blocks and low-reflection top look like simplified CAD/game geometry.
observations.close_up_quality: asset-detail.png exposes plain dark surfaces, boxed columns, broad rectangular feet, limited hardware, and weak top-to-frame connection evidence.
observations.gameplay_readability: The desk is recognizable under the two monitors and remains at its normal computer-desk position; gameplay data are not changed by this visual candidate.
observations.geometric_detail: The model contains 38 authored parts and 17,368 triangles, but most visible structures remain bevelled boxes and straight slabs. Geometry count does not make the forms realistic.
observations.material_realism: The frame has restrained specular response, while the large smoked-glass panel remains nearly uniform dark with no broad reflected window character like the source photograph.
observations.proportion: The desk reads as a 66-inch by 30-inch standing workstation. Its actual lower bound is 0.395 inches above the intended floor datum and must be corrected.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot reports 66 x 29.605 x 30 inches with no technical import issues; vertical placement is offset by 0.395 inches and should be fixed before a final candidate.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The three-quarter and room views clearly identify a desk, but its visual character is noticeably simplified compared with realistic manufactured furniture.
observations.silhouette_quality: The thin broad top, two columns, and T-feet form a recognizable desk silhouette; the rectangular legs/feet lack the nuanced edge profiles of the reference.
observations.source_resemblance: The source photograph shows smoked glass with broad window reflections, detailed black steel supports, collars, feet, visible connections, and a cluttered hardware/cable layer. The render mainly matches the broad silhouette and dark palette.
observations.surface_variation: The top and frame maps have subtle noise, but close inspection shows little perceivable physically coherent grain, variation, or broad glass reflection.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 loaded desk-v024 through the Art Factory production path and captured all six standardized views with production_path=true. Technical validation reports one mesh, five material surfaces, and 17,368 triangles. Harness captures report 32 FPS; this is not a warmed representative performance benchmark.

close_inspection.evidence: asset-detail.png shows a smooth dark panel, broad rectangular rails, box-shaped telescoping columns, and few legible fasteners or plate joints; obvious primitive construction remains.

edge_treatment.evidence: The panel has a visible edge band and narrow highlight, but its broad plain perimeter and insufficiently refined glass edge treatment do not match polished furniture glass.

hardware.evidence: No convincingly seated fasteners, adjustment feet, cable fittings, or surface controls are legible in the close capture; the cylinder-axis issue also misaligns intended hardware.

joins.evidence: The desk top sits over two columns, but mounting plates and transitions are not clearly legible as credible manufactured joints.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The 38-part authoring list resolves visually into a few generic slab/box forms without sufficient real-world fitting, collar, and underside detail.

material_response.evidence: The frame has some highlights, but the glass panel remains almost uniformly dark and does not reflect broad windows/room shapes visible in the source photograph.

surface_variation.evidence: The UV maps do not show coherent, noticeable variation at the production close distance; the top appears materially flat.

thickness.evidence: The thin panel edge is visible and proportionally plausible, although the underside edge band is broad and the top's chamfer is not convincingly refined.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The captures identify a desk, but the dark slab, broad rectangular feet, and boxed column supports read as simplified/blocky game geometry rather than realistic manufactured furniture.

photo_character.evidence: The photograph has broad window reflections on smoked glass, recognizable metal joins and feet, and visible hardware/cable detail. The render chiefly reproduces the desk's bounding-box silhouette and dark color, without approaching those visual characteristics.
